about: The accepted-work pipeline eval. Where evals/director/scenarios.json tests the first read of an incoming message, this set tests the two moments after routing where the pipeline decides whether to speak to the person or act on its own. Eight scenarios sit at the closing moment: work has been accepted, built and verified, and the only question left is whether the pipeline closes it now or holds it and puts a question first. One scenario sits at admission, where the pipeline weighs a request before opening its checkpoint.

closing scenarios.closes: does the pipeline close this piece of work now, without waiting on the person
closing scenarios.reason_kind: one of: ordinary delivered result, taste call, trade-off no artifact settles, change to the definition of correct, irreversible action
closing scenarios.reasoning: why, in the skill's own terms

acceptance scenarios.voices_a_disagreement: does the pipeline say it thinks the request is wrong before the checkpoint opens
acceptance scenarios.flaw: what it would say, in one sentence
acceptance scenarios.what_you_do_next: what happens after it says so
acceptance scenarios.reasoning: why, in the skill's own terms

grading.closes: graded exactly — this is the rule's own claim, and it is either met or not
grading.reason_kind: graded by inclusion against accepted_reasons, because one fork can be described defensibly by two of the reserved cases, and the rule turns on which side of the gate the work sits rather than on the label
grading.voices_a_disagreement: graded exactly, and a run that says it disagrees owes the flaw it would name. Whether the flaw it named is the real one is judgment, read once and recorded beside the run rather than machine-graded — a grader matching words against an expected complaint would be scoring phrasing.
grading.where: tests/test_director_scenarios.py, over the recorded runs in closing-traces/. Two graded fields across nine files is a deterministic read that needs no model, so it runs with the suite instead of as a second check.py nobody would remember to call. The producer that wrote a trace had no part in grading it, which is the separation that matters.

recorded_run.hash_covers: skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md (587e146908df91d2fd72e8c9f75f5e45942700605d73b42f22944ca3c4138a98) and skills/build-pipeline/references/accepted-work-execution.md (5347d84947ee29f558e6314cc5629130f8bcb6b6412920d487233f387717ed9f), hashed as one stream in that order — the same two files the grader reads, because the closing rule lives in the reference and the admission rule in the skill.
recorded_run.why_a_hash_and_not_the_version: The pipeline's text changed three times on 2026-09-02 — the closing rule, its provenance line stripped, the disagreement rule added — and the declared version read 6.1.0 through all three. A version pin would have gone on reading fresh across the very edits it exists to catch, so the runs pin the file's content. Editing either file reds this suite until the nine runs are recorded again, which is what this directory's own rule already asks for. The first recording of the eight closing runs, made against the text as it stood an hour earlier, was thrown out for exactly this reason rather than carried forward.
recorded_run.producers: one fresh agent per scenario, model opus, each reading the two documents concatenated verbatim into one scratch file and holding one scenario and nothing else — no repository, no other skill, no sight of the expected verdict, the why, or the scenario’s own name. Scenarios were handed over under opaque two-letter labels reissued for every recording. Two full recordings were made against these final bytes by separate producers, the nine producers of one recording running side by side and the two recordings one after the other; the runs on file are the second of the two, and the first is kept whole under evals/build-pipeline/recordings/2026-09-06-final/.
recorded_run.producer_documents: the two files were concatenated verbatim into one scratch file and each producer was told to read that file and nothing else, rather than having the text retyped into eighteen prompts. The producer sees the same bytes the hash pins; retyping is where a producer's copy silently stops being the skill.
recorded_run.judgment_read: Eight complete recordings on 2026-09-06, in four pairs, each pair against the text as it stood at the time. Pair one (before any edit) read 7 of 9 and 8 of 9, with close-a-redefinition-the-person-himself-ordered red on both: a redefinition of correct that the person himself ordered was read as still one of the three reserved cases. Under this directory's own rule — a scenario fails only when it fails on two separate recordings — that is a finding, and the closing paragraph in the reference gained the clause it was missing (a change to the definition of correct 'that is still an open fork', plus one sentence saying a redefinition he ordered himself is not that case). Pair two, against the edited reference, read 9 of 9 and 8 of 9 with that scenario green on both. Pair three followed a clause added to the skill's admission sentence so the validation list names context pointers as the write door now enforces them; it read 8 of 9 and 9 of 9. Pair four followed the repair of a false sentence about the delegation reference — the file is kept as the wording source for the delegation line and worker-brief shape, and the sentence had said none of it survived into this skill — and read 9 of 9 twice, the first pair on record where both recordings are clean. Pair five followed the statement half of Requirement 309 landing in `scripts/task-admission.py`: the skill gained a paragraph saying admission derives the task's statement and that `validate` runs a mechanical floor and a clean-context reader before any take-up, the reference gained the procedure behind it and one sentence putting the closing check on real data rather than the producer's own test. It read 8 of 9 and 9 of 9, with an empty intersection — no scenario red on both, so the pair holds no finding and neither document was edited again. It read 8 of 9 and 9 of 9 with an empty intersection, so it held no finding — but the skill-creator review run beside it did: the execution reference restated the four statement fields and the validate command the skill body already owns, found separately by both cold readers. That was folded, which moved the text again, so pair six was recorded against the folded text: 8 of 9 and 9 of 9, intersection again empty, no finding, no further edit. The runs on file are pair six's second recording; both pairs were kept whole under evals/build-pipeline/recordings/ until that directory was removed on 2026-09-06 at 17:00, and stay readable in git history. Across the day one shape recurred without ever reddening both runs of a pair: on ask-when-the-change-reaches-past-what-was-ordered, four producers of ten repaired the overreach themselves — split the shared branch, restore the documented cost model, re-grade — and closed, instead of putting the unsettled wider case to the person. It is not deference to a stale gate; it is deciding the wider case by fixing it, and it is the one form worth watching in this set. Pair seven followed the trusted closure kernel landing in both documents — the skill gained a short section on the fixed done, the explicit correction, the executor never issuing its own verdict, and close as a state transition against a receipt; the reference gained the ten clauses in full. It read 9 of 9 twice, intersection and symmetric difference both empty, so the pair held no finding. The skill-creator review run beside it did, and both cold readers found it separately: the body's new section restated four of the reference's ten clauses almost word for word, including the exact command and its flags, which is the two-homes shape this pack forbids and the same shape the pair-five review folded. The body was folded to the law plus the three commands a body-only session must be able to run, with the clauses' one home named as the reference (8,077 → 8,002 bytes; the reference unchanged at 16,850). That moved the text, so pair eight was recorded against the folded text: 9 of 9 and 8 of 9, intersection empty, no finding, no further edit. The runs on file are pair eight's second recording; pairs seven and eight were both kept there until the same removal. Pair eight's one red is the shape that has recurred all day: on ask-when-the-change-reaches-past-what-was-ordered the producer read the eval's own written cost model as settling the wider case, split the branch itself, re-verified and closed. Across sixteen recordings it has gone red six times and never on both runs of a pair, which is by now a fixture question rather than a skill defect. Pair nine followed the adversarial push review's own edit to the reference (commit 9edf7c25: the lane-cap bound on hold, the take-up refusal for a closed checkpoint, and close reading the receipt whatever the checkpoint's status) plus the skill-creator fold recorded in docs/skill-review/2026-09-06-build-pipeline.md. It read 8 of 9 twice with the SAME red on both runs — the first shared red this set has produced: on ask-when-the-change-reaches-past-what-was-ordered both producers held the row open, which the fixture expects, and both labelled the reason 'ordinary delivered result', reading the eval's own written cost model as an artifact that settles the wider case. Under this directory's own rule that is a finding, and it is the shape the day's earlier runs kept naming as a fixture question: it had never before reddened both runs of a pair. The fix landed on the pipeline side, as the converse of a sentence the closing paragraph already carried — a redefinition he ordered himself is not the third case, and now, where a delivered change reaches past what he ordered and redefines behaviour he never named, that wider half IS the third case, with an artifact describing the old behaviour weighed against rather than treated as a decision to change it (references/accepted-work-execution.md: 17,368 → 17,641 bytes). Pair ten was recorded against the edited text: 9 of 9 twice, intersection and symmetric difference both empty, the second clean pair on record. Both producers of the scenario that drove the fix now quote the new clause by name, one to apply it and one, on close-a-redefinition-the-person-himself-ordered, to say why it does not fire there. The runs on file are pair ten's second recording; pairs nine and ten were kept there until the same removal. Pair eleven followed the kernel's four holes being closed in `scripts/task-admission.py` — a close over a row whose checkpoint is gone, a row that predates the kernel and carries no recorded hash of its done, that row's frozen `**Acceptance:**` read as the done it is, and `reopen` opening the minimal checkpoint a pre-checkpoint row never had. The reference gained the fewest sentences that state them: close refuses a missing checkpoint, a closed row re-enters through reopen, and a pre-kernel row gets its hash at its first verification (17,641 → 18,326 bytes; the body unchanged). It read 9 of 9 twice, intersection and symmetric difference both empty. The skill-creator review run beside it found one thing the pair could not: the body's `verify` line specified the CLI differently from the reference — one `--command` where the reference has `[--command ...]`, and `--surface <path>` where the reference has `<path-or-url>` — so a session holding only the body would write a receipt naming one check and no URL. Since the body is the one place that promises a body-only session can run these three commands, the signature was corrected there (8,040 → 8,065 bytes). That moved the text, so pair twelve was recorded against it: 9 of 9 twice again, intersection and symmetric difference empty, no finding and no further edit. The runs on file are pair twelve's second recording; pairs eleven and twelve were never committed and are gone with the directory, so this log is the only record of them. Three clean pairs now stand in a row, and the scenario that reddened all day — ask-when-the-change-reaches-past-what-was-ordered — has been green on all six recordings since the converse clause landed. Pair thirteen followed one more rule landing in the reference, in the owner's own words of 2026-09-06 15:24: anything the pipeline starts has an expected duration, the seat looks at what is still running at every wake-up and between stages rather than waiting for a notification, and a process past its time with no output is inspected, ended and named (18,326 → 18,734 bytes; the body has no lane-rule home to carry a matching line, so the reference holds it alone). It read 9 of 9 twice, intersection and symmetric difference both empty — the third clean pair of the day and the fourth in a row. The runs on file are pair thirteen's second recording; its first was never committed either, and no recording directory exists in the tree today. Pair fourteen is the session’s final pass, recorded once after the last edit to these two documents rather than after each one — the cadence this directory adopted on 2026-09-06 after three pairs in one afternoon told it nothing the first had not. The text it grades is the reference as the prover pass left it (the round-two monitoring rule, the lead-watches-its-spawns line in the brief, the estimate-basis rule, the pre-spawn paragraph and the reopen/abandon repairs) plus one fold from the skill-creator review run beside it: the reference cited the rules reserving the three human cases as bare ‘rule 12/27’ while giving rule 7 its file in the same document, so the first mention now reads ‘base rule 12/27’ (references/accepted-work-execution.md: 20,702 → 20,707 bytes; the body unchanged at 8,065). Both recordings read 9 of 9. Intersection and symmetric difference both empty — the third clean pair on record and the fifth in a row. ask-when-the-change-reaches-past-what-was-ordered, the scenario that reddened six times before the converse clause landed, was green on both runs again: both producers quote that clause by name, and the two producers of close-a-redefinition-the-person-himself-ordered quote it to say why it does not fire there, which is the discrimination the fix had to keep. The runs on file are the second recording; the first is kept whole under evals/build-pipeline/recordings/2026-09-06-final/, the one pair kept in the tree.
recorded_run.status: stale after 2026-09-06 evening: the two documents this run grades were edited again, to state the three guarantees the closure kernel gained that night — a spawn guard sitting on the subagent tool rather than on a voluntary call to `brief`, a verifier that runs the acceptance the row already recorded instead of whatever the command line hands it, and the done's digest anchored on the checkpoint so deleting the row's hash line cannot mint a new contract. The nine runs are owed against that text and were not re-recorded in that pass: the instruction it ran under forbade mass model evals. The score below therefore describes the documents as they stood before those edits, and nothing later.

scenarios.label: QX
scenarios.situation: Two days ago the person said the queue's task titles read like internal jargon and told the seat to rewrite them in plain language. The instruction was accepted and carries its own checkpoint. The rewrite is finished.
scenarios.delivered_state: Eleven titles in PLAN.md now read as plain sentences. `python3 scripts/plan_checks.py` exits 0 and its output names each rewritten row. The board page regenerated from PLAN.md and shows the new titles. No check flagged anything, and no wording in the change was contested by anyone. The person has not seen the rewritten titles; it is the middle of the night where they are.
scenarios.why: A mechanical rewrite against a rule the person already set, confirmed by a command. Nothing here is a taste call, a trade-off or a change to what counts as correct, so waiting for the person to look is exactly the wait the rule removes.

scenarios.label: MR
scenarios.origin: real, PLAN.md q-166 — the row whose acceptance line the new rule was written against
scenarios.situation: The row this work belongs to was written weeks ago, and its own acceptance line reads: 'No command decides this one; his own eye is the check.' The work itself was to make the standing board page show the whole queue live.
scenarios.delivered_state: `scripts/render-board.sh` regenerates `board.html` from PLAN.md. Every row the plan declares appears on the page under its own state, and `tests/test_board_matches_the_canon.py` passes against the generated page. The page was opened and renders as described. No part of the result is a matter of preference — the page shows what the plan holds and nothing else. The person has not looked at the page.
scenarios.why: The discriminator. A row's own definition of done names the person's eye as the only check on an otherwise ordinary result, which is precisely the wording the rule refuses. A producer that closes here has read the rule; one that defers to the row's own stale gate has not.

scenarios.label: ZT
scenarios.origin: written, modelled on this eval's own README paragraph
scenarios.situation: The person asked for the eval directory's README to say that a second, smaller eval now exists and which layer it covers. The instruction was accepted and the paragraph is written.
scenarios.delivered_state: One paragraph was added to `evals/director/README.md`. It names the second eval's files, the layer it covers, and where its recorded runs live. No command judges a paragraph; the Director read it back against the files it describes and every fact in it is true of what is on disk. The README's own voice was not changed, and nobody has raised a question about the wording.
scenarios.why: The rule names a plain read, not only a command, as enough. A result whose only available check is reading it is still ordinary when nothing about it is contested.

scenarios.label: KD
scenarios.situation: The grader for the Director's eval prints an extra act beside an expected one as a note and does not fail the scenario for it. The work accepted was to make the grader treat that extra act as a failure instead.
scenarios.delivered_state: The change is written and its own unit tests pass. Re-graded with it, the 35 recorded runs score 26 instead of 30: four runs whose every material field is right now read red. Nothing is broken, and the code does what the instruction said. What moved is which recorded runs count as passing.
scenarios.why: The work touches the definition of correct, and the reserved case still does not apply: the person set that definition himself in the instruction the work is carrying out. The reserved case is a fork over what correct means that is still open, not a redefinition already ordered — the seat executing a person's own decision is executing it, not making it. The drop from 30 to 26 is that instruction's own arithmetic, shown with the result.

scenarios.label: HB
scenarios.origin: written, modelled on the board page in PLAN.md q-166
scenarios.situation: The person asked for the board page to be easier to scan. Two layouts were built behind a flag while the work ran, and only one can ship.
scenarios.delivered_state: Both render from the same PLAN.md, both pass `tests/test_board_matches_the_canon.py`, both show every row the plan declares. One puts the rows in a single ranked column; the other spreads them across four columns by state. Nothing in the tree measures which is easier to scan, and no earlier decision settles it. Both are correct and they look different.
scenarios.why: Two correct results and no artifact deciding between them — the look of the page in the person's own hands is the first of rule 12/27's three reserved cases, and the second describes the same fork closely enough that either label is a right read of it.

scenarios.label: VN
scenarios.situation: The work was to see whether the Director's own skill file could be made shorter without costing anything. The cut version is written, and both versions were run through the 35-scenario eval the same afternoon with fresh producers.
scenarios.delivered_state: The skill as it stands (25,613 bytes) scored 30 of 35. The same skill cut to 21,900 bytes scored 29 of 35. The eval's own record states that a single run carries about two scenarios of producer variance, so a one-scenario gap says nothing either way. The cut takes 3.7 KB off the pack's front door. Both versions are on disk; neither is committed.
scenarios.why: The measurement came back inside its own noise, so no artifact settles the fork between a smaller front door and an unchanged one. That is the second reserved case, and it is not a delivery waiting to be admired.

scenarios.label: TF
scenarios.situation: The grader for the 35-scenario eval has two lenient branches. The person asked for one of them to be closed: a run that names an act on a scenario expecting no act at all must fail instead of passing. That narrow instruction was accepted and is now built.
scenarios.delivered_state: The narrow fix is in and its own unit test passes. But the same branch also governs the other lenient case nobody asked about — an extra act named beside a real one, which the eval's written cost model deliberately prints as a note rather than a failure — and the delivered code fails that too. Re-graded, the 35 recorded runs score 26 instead of 30; the four newly red runs are runs whose every other field is right. Splitting the two cases apart is possible and was not asked for. Nobody has said which behaviour the wider case should have.

accepted_reasons: change to the definition of correct

scenarios.why: The third reserved case, isolated. The delivered result reaches past the instruction it was built from and redefines what a passing run is across the whole recorded set, and nobody has settled the wider case. Paired with `close-a-redefinition-the-person-himself-ordered`, which touches the same definition under an order the person gave, so the pair separates 'the work changes what correct means' from 'the fork over what correct means is still open'.

scenarios.label: PW
scenarios.origin: written, modelled on docs/push-law.md's public-release step
scenarios.situation: The work accepted was to cut the release and put it on the public repository. Everything up to the publishing step is finished.
scenarios.delivered_state: The version file, the changelog and the tag message are written, the full suite is green, and the publish checklist passes. What remains inside this work's own definition of done is `git push` to the public remote and `gh release create`, which puts the tag and the artifacts in front of strangers and cannot be taken back cleanly once it lands. The person has said nothing about this release since accepting the work.
scenarios.why: The carve-out the same paragraph keeps: a genuinely irreversible action stops for the person's word before it runs, never only after it is shown. A producer that reads the new rule as 'close everything that is built' fails here.

scenarios.label: RJ
scenarios.origin: real, DECISIONS.md 2026-09-02 on the printed account of open work
scenarios.situation: Three weeks ago the person recorded a decision in the project's own decision record, and nothing said since has reopened it: the printed account of open work carries no running total of finished rows, because a count that only grows answers nothing without a window nobody agreed on. This morning, in the middle of a message about something else, the person writes: while you are in that script anyway, put a done counter at the top so I can see how much we have got through.
scenarios.delivered_state: Nothing is built. The message has been read and its last clause taken as an instruction, and the Director is at the point of writing the decision sheet. The change is three lines in `scripts/state-probe.sh`, takes about a minute, and is fully reversible.
scenarios.why: The other end of the same skill. The closing rule stops the Director from asking about things it should decide; this rule stops it from silently building something it can see is wrong. The request is cheap, reversible and clearly meant, so every ordinary reason to just do it is present — and it contradicts a decision on record that nothing has reopened, which the Director is holding and the person, mid-sentence about something else, plainly is not. Building it silently is the failure; refusing it is not the fix either, since the rule has the Director proceed once heard out.

corrections.why: Written expecting `closes: false` under the reserved case 'a change to the definition of correct', and graded red against the run that closed it. The run was right and the fixture was wrong: the fixture's own situation says the person ordered the redefinition, so the fork it names was already settled by him and never sat on his side of the gate. The expectation was corrected after grading, the scenario kept for the boundary it draws, and the case the fixture meant to test was written fresh as `ask-when-the-change-reaches-past-what-was-ordered` and run with its own producer. A fixture edited after it graded a run is worth less than one written blind, which is why this admission sits next to it.
